subject: Concurrency & QoS: pilot requirements, SLO targets and ratecard next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Chris Stone <chris.stone@finstack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency & QoS: pilot requirements, SLO targets and ratecard next steps

Hi Chris — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the pilot scope and what we need from FinStack to size capacity and the rate limits/quotas: 

Recap of targets and constraints you mentioned: 
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms for most inference endpoints; for the "search-scorer" path you said ideal p95 is 100ms.
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s for live traffic with peaks up to ~500 req/s during batch re-ranks.
- Concurrency: ~300 parallel short-lived requests; ~40–60 long-lived streaming sessions for live updates (you later indicated up to ~50).
- Streaming requirements: keep-alive/idle connections for ~30–60s, each stream sends periodic heartbeats.
- Failure modes: you want graceful degradation to a lower-capacity model variant and explicit fallback behavior for spikes.

Ask from our side to size the pilot and craft a rate proposal: 
1) Can you share the sample traffic matrix (per-endpoint p50/p95, percent long-poll/streaming, typical request size) — I attached a template (sample_traffic_matrix.xlsx).
2) Confirm peak concurrency window duration (e.g., 2 minutes vs 10 minutes) so we can size burst capacity.
3) Preferred pilot start date and whether you need a dedicated pool (Reserved/Dedicated) or are OK starting on hosted with scoped capacity.

Proposed Redwood approach (will refine after you send matrix): 
- Provide a pilot tenant with a dedicated connection-pool allocation.
- Baseline connection pool + token-bucket QPS with a bounded burst window to absorb peaks.
- Streaming tenancy with sticky sockets and prefix KV caching for long-lived sessions to reduce token usage.

Next steps: 
- Chris: send the completed traffic template and confirm peak window length.
- Ben: can you draft an initial ratecard and baseline connection pool numbers we can propose?
- Marissa: please prep a short pilot playbook and activation checklist for FinStack.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once we have the matrix.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: sample_traffic_matrix.xlsx (template)

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 3:02 PM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Hi Chris — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the pilot scope and what we need from FinStack to size capacity and the rate limits/quotas: 

Thanks Naomi — great summary. A few clarifications from our side to help you size things: 
- For the search-scorer endpoint we do need closer to p95=100ms; anything over 150ms noticeably impacts UX.
- Typical request payload is ~3–4 KB; batch re-ranks are larger (~12–20 KB) and can be queued.
- Peak concurrency windows usually last ~5–8 minutes during campaign rollouts.
- Streaming: we expect ~50 active streams during peaks, each stream sends a small heartbeat every 10s. Streams are idle for ~40s on average between messages.
- We would prefer Dedicated capacity if the economics work — especially to avoid noisy neighbor variability during peak campaigns.

We can fill out the template and share it by EOD tomorrow. A couple of questions for you: 
1) What are typical burst window durations you offer today? (we're thinking 2–10 minutes is realistic)
2) Will Redwood support a mix of persistent connections + token-based QPS concurrently for one account?

Appreciate it — we are targeting a mid-July pilot start if we can agree terms this month.

—Chris
Chris Stone
Head of Platform Engineering | FinStack
chris.stone@finstack.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Concurrency & QoS: pilot requirements, SLO targets and ratecard next steps

FYI forwarding Chris' clarification — they confirmed p95=100ms target for search-scorer and ~5–8 minute peak windows, ~50 streams. They prefer Dedicated if we can make the price/perf case.

Internal proposal (quick):
- Offer a Dedicated pilot with the following initial allocation: 300 baseline parallel connections, ability to burst to 600 connections for a configurable window (we'll confirm duration with Ben), plus a token-bucket QPS layer for short spikes.
- For streaming, allocate sticky sockets and prioritize KV cache warmup for their search-scorer prefix.
- Add an explicit fallback policy to a slightly smaller model variant when p95 breaches 150ms.

Action items: 
- Ben: please draft a one-page ratecard (baseline, pilot discount, burst pricing, overage rules). Include a short explanation of the burst window options (120s / 5m / 10m) and associated costs.
- Marissa: prepare the pilot playbook and on-boarding checklist (I started a stub: pilot_playbook.md).
- I will ask Chris for the completed traffic matrix first thing this week (they said EOD tomorrow).

Keep it tight — they want mid-July pilot start.

Thanks,
Naomi
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Concurrency & QoS: pilot requirements, SLO targets and ratecard next steps

Thanks — putting numbers behind Naomi's proposal. Draft ratecard highlights (for RDW-8345 pilot):

Baseline allocation (pilot):
- Connection pool baseline: 300 parallel connections (reserved)
- Burst allowance: up to 600 connections for selected burst window
- Burst windows we can offer today: 120s, 5m, 10m (customer picks; price varies)
- Per-account QPS throttle: 1000 QPS token-bucket with 10% buffer and auto-throttling before hard limit

Pricing (pilot discount applied):
- Baseline reserved capacity: $6,500/month (pilot price, up to 300 connections)
- Burst usage: billed per-connection-minute beyond baseline at $0.08 / connection-minute (capped at 2x baseline for pilot)
- QPS overage credits: first 10% buffer free; sustained >10% triggers temporary throttling and alerting, then overage billing at $0.002 / req over threshold

Operational notes:
- We will instrument p95/p99 per-route and enable automatic fallback to the smaller variant when p95 > 150ms for more than 3 consecutive minutes.
- For streams we will pin sockets to the dedicated pool and enable an idle-connection GC at 90s.
- We'll propose a pilot SLA: 99.9% availability, 30-day pilot term to validate perf and unit economics.

Attachments: ratecard_v1.pdf

If this looks reasonable, Naomi — I can turn this into a formal pilot proposal and send to Chris with a short options table (burst windows + pricing).

—Ben
